transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Aegis - Head of ML), Maya Chen (Aegis - Platform Eng), Tom Alvarez (Aegis - Security)

Summary (auto): Onboarding progress, access still blocked by VPN and KMS perms, Redwood asked to run short latency/cost benchmark once infra access is resolved.

00:00 - Sam Carter: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync. Can you all hear me okay?
00:05 - Maya Chen: Yep loud and clear, thanks Sam.
00:12 - Luis Ortega: Yep, good here. Quick note, I have to hop off at 15:40 so I might miss the last five.
00:20 - Sam Carter: Noted, thanks Luis. Priya and I will run through the access checklist and the initial numbers we pulled from the Dedicated trial nodes.
00:35 - Priya Nair: Hi team, I have the small bench results, they're rough but useful. Quick reminder this is from the dedicated nodes in us-west and the tests used the 8k context Redwood-3b model variant, might be noisy.
00:50 - Tom Alvarez: Just before you jump in, has anyone had a chance to look at the network diagram we requested? I sent a snippet yesterday.
00:58 - Maya Chen: We saw it, Tom. But infra needs the full diagram with port ranges. That's part of why the VPN tunnel isn't up yet.
01:10 - Sam Carter: OK that's fair. I'll make sure we send the full diagram and call out the firewall ports (443, 5230 for the agent heartbeat, etc). We'll also include a short note on IP ranges and suggestions for NAT configurations.
01:24 - Luis Ortega: Great. On the data side, we still need the KMS flow - can Redwood confirm if customer KMS is supported for private deployment?
01:32 - Priya Nair: Yes, we do support external KMS for Private and Dedicated via Vault/KMS integrations. I'll add an integration note and the minimal IAM perms needed. Sorry if that was unclear in the docs, some of the names get confusing - we call it Redwood Private KMS binder in the notes, which is dumb, we'll clarify.
01:52 - Maya Chen: Perfect, we'll need the actual policy lines so infra can apply them.
02:00 - Priya Nair: Absolutely, we'll paste the terraform snippet.
02:08 - Sam Carter: Priya, can you share the preliminary latency/cost numbers?
02:12 - Priya Nair: Sure. So these are synthetic throughput runs at batch size 8, sequence length ~512 tokens. p99 in us-west was about 140ms on the Dedicated 80GB A100 instances for the 3b variant, median around 40ms. Token cost estimates were approx $0.0009 per token after batching, which is an estimate — real numbers will depend on your prompt distribution and cache hit rates.
02:40 - Luis Ortega: That p99 seems higher than we'd like; are we seeing any KV cache misses or batch starvation?
02:48 - Priya Nair: Good question. In the short runs we saw some variance due to cold KV cache and small request bursts; if you enable prefix caching and increase concurrency we expect p99 to drop closer to ~100ms. There's also potential to quantize model to bf16 or 4-bit which helps cost but may affect quality; that's a tradeoff we can show in the benchmark.
03:14 - Tom Alvarez: When you say quantize, do you mean Redwood will run a quantized variant in the same endpoint, or is that a separate model endpoint?
03:22 - Priya Nair: It can be a separate variant we deploy and route to. We typically do canary rollouts: keep a stable float endpoint and route a percentage of traffic to the quantized variant to monitor regressions. We can automate fallbacks if quality drops.
03:44 - Maya Chen: Sounds good. Back to access - we still don't have the service account privileges for pulling secrets from our KMS. Maya to infra is working but needs exact role names.
03:56 - Sam Carter: We'll include the exact role names in the note. Also, do you prefer we share the SOC2 and network docs via the ticket or directly to the security mailing list?
04:05 - Tom Alvarez: Directly to the security mailing list please, cc me. That makes audits easier.
04:12 - Sam Carter: Noted. We'll send by Wednesday.
04:18 - Priya Nair: Another small item on the bench: we saw a small number of timeouts in the long sequence runs when concurrency spiked; switching to streaming reduces the tail a bit because tokens are pipelined, but it depends on client stack. Any restrictions on your side for streaming?
04:34 - Luis Ortega: We use an async streaming consumer in production, so streaming is fine. The bigger ask is, can Redwood support token-level tracing for debugging? We want to map latency to customer prompts.
04:46 - Priya Nair: We have tracing hooks and token-level metrics in Redwood Console; we can grant you a demo account to view per-route token latency and a small guide on how to interpret KV cache hit rates and batching histograms.
04:59 - Maya Chen: That demo account will be helpful.
05:03 - Sam Carter: Ok next, any blockers for the scheduled benchmark? We proposed next week, week of Nov 10.
05:10 - Luis Ortega: Main blocker is the VPN tunnel and service account perms. Once that's done, we can schedule. Also can Redwood run both hosted and dedicated variants in the run for side-by-side numbers?
05:21 - Priya Nair: Yes we can run both. For fairness we'll match concurrency and prompt set. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, token cost, and quality regression metrics against your golden prompts.
05:36 - Tom Alvarez: Speaking of prompts, Luis, can you confirm the subset you want used? We don't want production data to leak into logs.
05:44 - Luis Ortega: We'll provide anonymized prompt set and a sample of 1k queries. Also need to confirm retention: logs from the trial should not be kept beyond 30 days.
05:54 - Sam Carter: Redwood supports configurable retention. We'll confirm 30-day retention and redact logs in the benchmark run if you prefer.
06:02 - Maya Chen: Good. Any changes in SSO or RBAC we need to know?
06:08 - Priya Nair: For the pilot we'll create one sandbox org with RBAC. You can add users via SAML or invite emails. For production we'd do SAML/SCIM integration.
06:18 - Maya Chen: We'll start with invites in sandbox.
06:21 - Sam Carter: Cool. Quick note on costs: the $0.0009 per token is an estimate, and we'll refine once we have real prompt distribution. Also the burst pricing for Dedicated is different if you exceed reserved throughput. We'll share a small calc sheet.
06:38 - Luis Ortega: Please do, we want to show finance.
06:41 - Priya Nair: I'll attach a simple spreadsheet with the math — tokens per request * median tokens * monthly qps assumed.
06:49 - Sam Carter: Any security items we missed?
06:52 - Tom Alvarez: Just audit logs: we need proof that audit logs are immutable and retained. Do you ship to our S3 bucket or do you host redwood logs?
06:59 - Priya Nair: We can push audit logs to your S3 with server-side encryption. For enterprise private deployments folks usually prefer pushing to customer-managed storage. We'll include that option in the doc.
07:12 - Maya Chen: That should work. My infra engineer will set up the S3 bucket with the policy.
07:16 - Luis Ortega: One other small thing — can Redwood provide a short troubleshooting playbook for common failures like KV cache warming and OOMs?
07:24 - Priya Nair: Yes, a 1-page playbook is doable. We'll include steps: clear cache, warm cache with prefix sets, increase concurrency, fallback to smaller model.
07:36 - Sam Carter: Great. Let's recap action items and owners. Priya will run the benchmark plan and scripts and lead the run. Sam will send SOC2, network diagram, and KMS snippet. Maya will get service account perms and create S3 bucket. Luis will supply anonymized prompts and success criteria. Tom will confirm the security mailing list for docs.
07:58 - Maya Chen: Confirmed.
08:01 - Luis Ortega: Confirmed, I'll try to be on the benchmark run but if not I'll review the results.
08:06 - Tom Alvarez: I'll be on the security call next week.
08:10 - Sam Carter: OK, thanks everyone. We'll send those docs and follow up with the benchmark calendar invite after infra items are clear.
08:18 - Priya Nair: Thanks team, we'll keep this short next week.
08:22 - Meeting end
